items.html:
Use the actual stored positive (D) as an exact change of coordinates. Its rounded construction needs no separate correction. Define [ B_0=D^{-1}AD,\qquad x_*=A^{-1}t,\qquad r_0=D^{-1}(t-A\widehat x). ] Here (A,t,\widehat x,D) mean the exact values encoded by their stored floats.

For selected physical incident coefficients (p), define (t=Tp) using the encoded (T,p). Evaluate that multiplication in the residual precision too.

  1. Preferred certificate. If a verified upper bound (q\ge|I-B_0|\infty) satisfies (q<1), then [ \boxed{|D^{-1}(\widehat x-x*)|\infty \le\frac{|r_0|\infty}{1-q}.} ] Failure of (q<1) means this certificate failed; it does not establish ill-conditioning.

  2. When (q\ge1), reuse the LU factorization to compute an approximate inverse (R\approx\widehat B^{-1}). Certify [ \eta\ge|I-RB_0|\infty,\qquad \eta<1. ] Then [ \boxed{|D^{-1}(\widehat x-x*)|\infty \le\frac{|Rr_0|\infty}{1-\eta} \le\frac{|R|\infty|r_0|\infty}{1-\eta}.} ] This also proves nonsingularity. It is the approximate-inverse residual certificate in Rump, Verification methods, Theorem 10.2; the same Neumann-series argument applies over (\mathbb C).

    One additional dense inverse solve and defect product suffice; high precision is needed only for selected residuals, not a full high-precision factorization. An (2688^2) complex128 matrix occupies 110.25 MiB. Runtime on four threads remains unmeasured.

  3. Transfer certificates from rounded scaling explicitly. With [ \delta_B\ge|\widehat B-B_0|\infty, ] valid denominators use [ q\le|I-\widehat B|\infty+\delta_B, ] or [ \eta\le|I-R\widehat B|\infty+|R|\infty\delta_B. ] Original-equation residuals automatically include rounded (\widehat C), scaling, and final (\widehat x) construction errors. They do not automatically correct a stability denominator computed for (\widehat B).

  4. “Certified” requires arithmetic enclosures. Longdouble/mpmath evaluation alone supplies strong numerical evidence. Include upper bounds for residual, defect, norm, and scaling evaluation errors before calling the result certified.

    A practical dense-defect enclosure can use four real GEMMs. Under conventional floating-point arithmetic without overflow/underflow, with [ m(M)=\max_i\sum_j(|\Re M_{ij}|+|\Im M_{ij}|),\quad \gamma_k=\frac{ku}{1-ku}, ] their product/combine/subtract computation (\widehat E\approx I-R\widehat B) admits the conservative bound [ |I-R\widehat B|\infty \le |\widehat E|\infty+ \gamma_{n+2}\bigl[1+m(R)m(\widehat B)\bigr]. ] Evaluate the scalar bounds with outward rounding. Otherwise report an a posteriori error estimate, with the unverified arithmetic margin identified.

  5. Interpretation and solver comparison. If the weighted bound is (\varepsilon), then [ |\widehat x_i-x_{,i}|\le d_i\varepsilon,\qquad |\widehat x-x_|\infty\le d{\max}\varepsilon. ] If (\varepsilon<|D^{-1}\widehat x|\infty), weighted relative error is bounded by [ \frac{\varepsilon} {|D^{-1}\widehat x|\infty-\varepsilon}. ] For a certified reference and raw result evaluated against the same (A,T,D), [ |D^{-1}(x_{\rm raw}-x_*)|\infty \ge \max!\left(0,, |D^{-1}(x{\rm raw}-x_{\rm ref})|\infty-\varepsilon{\rm ref} \right). ] This can establish raw-LU inaccuracy; a large upper error bound alone cannot.

  6. Scope. These bounds concern the encoded upstream-(A)/local-(T) system. They exclude upstream assembly error, truncation error, and physical-model error. Selected RHS checks certify those responses only.

Minimal checks:

  • (A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\1&3\end{pmatrix}), (D=\mathrm{diag}(3,7)), (t=(1,1)^T), exact (x_*=(2/5,1/5)^T): exercise scaling corrections and check the bound against exact rational arithmetic.
  • (B=2I): (q=1) fails, while (R=\tfrac12I) gives (\eta=0).
  • Deliberately perturb the reference solution and verify both the error upper bound and the raw/reference lower-bound inequality.
